title: Where Pontotoc County households can get help with winter heating bills
excerpt: Applications start online. LIFT’s Highway 15 office handles the local appointment, and eligible households receive a credit through their energy provider.

facts.statement: Pontotoc County residents who need help paying for heat this winter can start an application online and finish it with LIFT, the community action agency serving the county. Its Pontotoc office is at 1597 Highway 15 North. The local number for questions about energy assistance or an appointment is 662-489-7329.
facts.evidence: State Community Services directory lists LIFT’s Pontotoc street address and number. The association lists Pontotoc in its service area. MDHS identifies the two-stage application process.
facts.date_context: Winter 2026–27 service information checked Nov. 25, 2026. Federal fiscal 2027 award dated Oct. 9, 2026.
facts.identities: LIFT, Inc.; Mississippi Department of Human Services; U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.

paragraphs.text: Pontotoc County residents who need help paying for heat this winter can start an application online and finish it with LIFT, the community action agency serving the county. Its Pontotoc office is at 1597 Highway 15 North. The local number for questions about energy assistance or an appointment is 662-489-7329.

On the Access MS portal, select “Community Services” to start the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program pre-application. Watch for a letter or email giving the date of the in-person appointment and listing the documents to bring. The state says to keep the appointment even if some paperwork is missing. The agency can give applicants time to supply it afterward.

The state gives priority to households with an older adult, a person with a disability or a child age 5 or younger. It says those applicants should expect an appointment within 30 business days of applying. For other households, the stated window is 45 days. The appointment notice comes before a decision on assistance.

Assistance can cover heat from sources including electricity, natural gas, propane and wood. When an application is approved, the agency pays the energy provider directly and the household sees a credit on its bill. Federal records show an Oct. 9 award of $31,855,822 to Mississippi for the program statewide. Local assistance depends on funds being available.
